definition: A model that generates sequences one element at a time, with each new element conditioned on all previously generated elements.
details: Most modern LLMs are autoregressive: they generate text token-by-token, feeding each generated token back in as part of the context for predicting the next one.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. Here is the short version: A model that generates sequences one element at a time, with each new element conditioned on all previously generated elements. The part that makes it sing: Most modern LLMs are autoregressive: they generate text token-by-token, feeding each generated token back in as part of the context for predicting the next one. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. And that is Autoregressive Model — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
